newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM'S UNIONS DEMAND PAY RISE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH KGHM COPPER FIRM'S UNIONS DEMAND PAY RISE.

text.p: The Solidarity trade union in Poland's KGHM copper concern went on strike alert on Monday after the government failed to appoint a mediator in its pay-rise talks with the firm's board, KGHM's spokesman said.
Piotr Bielawski told Reuters Solidarity demanded a monthly rise of 150 zlotys or 7.5 percent of the average pay for the company's 27,000 workers employed directly in production as of July 1.
"As of Monday the Solidarity union went on strike alert because the government has not yet appointed a mediator in their talks with the board," Bielawski said.

The second of KGHM's two biggest unions, the Union of Copper Industry Workers (ZZPPM), also demands wage increases, but only of 5.7 percent of the average wage in the company, now at 2,000 zlotys, its leader Ryszard Zbrzyzny said.
The average wage in Poland is 948 zlotys.
ZZPPM did not announce a strike alert because it has a government apppointed mediator.
KGHM's Solidarity officials were not immediately available for comment but ZZPPM's head Ryszard Zbrzyzny told Reuters he expected the dispute could be resolved by the end of the year.
"KGHM's president told us that the board would consider a rise after it reviews the firm's financial results for the first three quarters of the year," Zbrzyzny said.

"We demand the 5.7 percent rise because the minimum wage in Poland has risen by that much since July 1 and in our agreement with the management wages in the firm are linked to the level of the minimum wage," he said.
KGHM, one of the world's major copper and silver producers worth an estimated $2-3 billion, is slated for privatisation both on the domestic and foreign markets next year.
KGHM's Bielawski said that given the current low world copper prices rises for 27,000 employees involved in production were highly unlikely.
"Considering the current level of copper on world markets, any rise is unlikely this year," he said.
